objective.statement: Group short notes with beams so that the beats can be seen.
successCriteria: I beam quavers and semiquavers within a beat.
I do not join notes across a beat that should stay visible.
I can pick the bar whose beats are grouped clearly.

explanation.text: When a bar contains short notes, we join them with beams in groups that show the beat. This makes the music easy to read at a glance.

music.textAlternative: A bar of 4/4: two pairs of beamed quavers, then a minim.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: 2 beamed together (quaver, quaver), 2 beamed together (quaver, quaver), minim.

explanation.caption: Each pair of quavers is one beat, so each pair has its own beam.

music.textAlternative: The same bar with every quaver written with a flag and no beams.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: quaver, quaver, quaver, quaver, minim.

explanation.caption: The same rhythm with flags only is harder to read. Beam quavers in groups that fill a beat.

explanation.text: In 4/4, keep the middle of the bar visible: do not run a beam from beat 2 into beat 3. Start a new beam on each beat.
In 2/4, 3/4 and 4/4 each crotchet beat gets its own group: a pair of quavers, or four semiquavers.

music.textAlternative: One bar of 4/4: two beamed quavers, a crotchet, four beamed semiquavers and a crotchet.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: 2 beamed together (quaver, quaver), crotchet, 4 beamed together (semiquaver, semiquaver, semiquaver, semiquaver), crotchet.

steps: Play all and tap the beat. Each beam covers exactly one beat.
Beat one: two quavers. Beat two: a crotchet. Beat three: four semiquavers. Beat four: a crotchet.
Every beat is easy to find because the beams never run across a beat boundary.
demonstration.textAlternative: A bar of 4/4 with each beat shown separately: a beamed pair of quavers, a crotchet, four beamed semiquavers and a crotchet.

guided.prompt: These notes are grouped in a way that hides the beats. Join and split the beams so each beat is clear.

music.textAlternative: Bar 1: semiquaver, semiquaver, quaver, dotted quaver, semiquaver, crotchet, quaver, quaver.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: semiquaver, semiquaver, quaver, dotted quaver, semiquaver, crotchet, quaver, quaver.

hints: Mark where each beat starts.
In 4/4 don't hide the middle of the bar.
In 4/4 there are four crotchet beats. Beam the quavers (and shorter notes) beat by beat.

feedback.correct: Grouped so every beat is clear.

mistakes.beam-across-middle: In four-beat bars, keep the two halves of the bar visible — don't beam across the middle.
mistakes.rest-across-beat: That rest hides where a beat begins. Use one rest to finish the beat, and another for the next.
mistakes.half-bar-rest-misplaced: A two-beat rest can fill the first or second half of a four-beat bar, but not the middle two beats.
mistakes.tie-instead-of-dot: A dotted note says the same thing more simply here.
mistakes.compound-beat-hidden: In compound time each beat is a dotted note split into three. Group in threes so each beat shows.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. Mark where each beat starts, then regroup.

mistakes.bar-overfull: This bar holds more beats than the time signature allows. Count the beats again and remove the extra.
mistakes.bar-underfull: There's still room in this bar. Count how many beats are missing.
mistakes.grouping-obscures-beat: The beats add up, but it's hard to see where each beat starts. Regroup the notes so every beat is visible.
mistakes.unnecessary-tie: You can write those tied notes as a single note (or a dotted note). That's easier to read.
mistakes.rest-grouping: Each silent beat (or part-beat) normally gets its own rest. Split the silence along the beats.
